Revised assessment: The FOMC’s description of a strengthening labor market and moderate real activity, with inflation still below but edging toward the 2% objective, aligns with the New Keynesian view that well-anchored inflation expectations and a flattened Phillips curve limit near-term price pressures even as unemployment nears its natural rate (Friedman-Phelps; Woodford). The decision to keep policy accommodative, signal only gradual rate increases, and continue balance-sheet reinvestment is consistent with inflation-forecast targeting and the forward-guidance literature (Svensson; Christiano, Eichenbaum, and Evans), as well as with the Taylor principle’s emphasis on measured adjustments. Overall tone: cautiously positive.
